articleTitle: CiGeN 1.0: A Generative AI Enabled Medical Image Augmentation Pipeline for Deep Network Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Deep Learning methods have gained a significant momentum in medical image classification tasks, including many ranges of datasets. However, these datasets often suffer from class imbalance, where the minority class (e.g., diseased cases) is underrepresented. This imbalance leads to biased predictions, affecting the model's performance. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) offer a potential solution by generating synthetic images for the minority class, helping balance the dataset. Methodology: In this study we further evaluated our Deep Learning Model CoVaD-GAN with separate set of datasets to test the dynamics behind it. We applied a Deep Convolutional GAN (DCGAN) to generate synthetic images for underrepresented classes in the chest X-ray (CXR) and Break His histopathological dataset. Augmented synthetic images were made a part of training set, and the model's performance was evaluated before and after augmentation using VGG-16, ResNet-50 with necessary metric measures as accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were compared pre- and post-GAN augmentation. We also evaluated the quality of GAN-generated images using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and manual expert reviews. The results demonstrate significant improvements in model accuracy, sensitivity, and F1-scores after applying GAN-based augmentation. The use of GANs for data augmentation enhances the ability of deep learning models to generalize, particularly for minority classes. GAN-generated images were of high quality and contributed positively to model performance. The Proposed model (CiGeN 1.0) dynamically generalizes the other medical dataset introduced to it and derived a fair resulting diagnosis.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Emotion Classification and Personal Response Optimization Using SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Humans experience a range of emotions during connection and communication, and these feelings differ in complexity, meaning, and intensity. Although behavioral emotions can also be expressed through body language, tone of voice, facial expressions, and other means, it can be challenging to identify the emotions in people who are unable to do so. In these cases, brain signals can be used to identify the emotions. In this research, we used a signal that the human brain creates based on an emotion's state to classify the emotions. To identify emotions, we employed EEG Eight frequency band signals. Different emotions, including joyful, sad, angry, fear, surprise, neutral, and disgust, were explained and recognized through expressions. by playing five minutes of these seven Indian films that focus on emotions, measuring the intensity of each emotion using brain signals, and comparing the results to the subject's remark. For this, we selected 35 Indian movie clips based on seven emotions and 50 individuals between the ages of 18 and 50. In order to improve accuracy, we used two techniques for emotion detection: one for answering the questions and another for classifying brain signals using support vector machines.

articleTitle: Design and Deployment of Drone-Assisted Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of locating survivors and delivering health services in critical areas where regular communication systems are unavailable due to natural disasters or the lack of a conventional terrestrial network. In these situations, drones can be employed to establish a temporary network that efficiently covers large areas. Their ability to adapt to various signal environments makes them versatile tools for real-time response. We propose a new approach that utilizes drones to identify the locations of users and provide cellular coverage along with other emergency assistance. This method estimates the location of affected users based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI) measurements from users’ devices. Subsequently, we establish a drone-assisted cellular network that connects to the nearest functioning terrestrial base station, using the minimum number of drones necessary to cover all affected users and deliver their required data rates. Our simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in accurately locating users. It achieves more than a 45% reduction in the displacement of drones when searching for affected users, compared to the traditional "Sweep & Search" technique [1]. Additionally, a minimal number of drones are deployed to establish a UAV-assisted cellular network for emergency communications.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment of Global Temperature Anomalies Using Intelligence Frameworks: Evaluating the Impact of Socioeconomic Factors and with a Case Study on Heatstroke Deaths in India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Rising global temperatures due to climate change have significantly increased the risk of heat-related illnesses, particularly heatstroke, in various regions. As global warming continues, it is crucial to understand patterns in heatstroke occurrences to predict and address future impacts. This study uses Machine Learning (ML) techniques to explore the connection between increasing temperatures and heatstroke incidents. ML models analyze extensive datasets containing meteorological data, health records, and geographical variables to uncover correlations between temperature spikes and heatstroke prevalence. The research incorporates supervised learning models such as linear Regression, lasso regression, ridge regression and voting regressor to predict high-risk periods and regions vulnerable to heatstroke. Additionally, time-series analysis and Prophet model is used to forecast future heatstroke cases by identifying climate data trends. These models are trained and validated using historical temperature and heatstroke fatality data from different regions. Preliminary findings indicate that extreme heatwaves, along with humidity and urbanization factors, significantly contribute to heatstroke occurrences. This study, leveraging ML, aims to improve the ability to predict and prevent heat-related health crises, offering valuable insights for public health planning, early-warning systems, and climate adaptation strategies to protect populations from the adverse effects of global warming.

articleTitle: Bone Fracture Detection using CNN and VGG
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Technology has played a huge role in human evolution since time immemorial. Now it is not only limited to engineers and data scientists, but far beyond, to even medicine. With increasing load on medical professionals and healthcare systems, digitalization can come handy. The traditional X-ray imaging gives unclear images of bone components in tissue making it difficult for surgeons to diagnose. Using technology, accurate diagnosis can be achieved. This includes a series of steps comprising pre-processing, edge detection, feature extraction and machine learning classifications. Machine learning algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN) and Visual Geometry Group(VGG) were used on a dataset consisting of 9246 training, 506 test and 829 validation images with 0.95 and 0.85 accuracies respectively. The data loss for CNN was found to be 0.24 in comparison to 0.4 for VGG. So from statistical inference, CNN is better.

articleTitle: Effect of Ujjayi Pranayama on Thyroid Profile and Body Mass Index of Patients with Hypothyroidism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Enhancing thyroid function may be possible with Ujjayi pranayama practice. Aim: The current study determines to estimate the impact of Ujjain pranayama on body mass index and thyroid profile. Setting and Design: Thirty hypothyroid patients from the primary health centre participated in the study, which used an experimental research approach. Methods and Materials: After explaining the goal of the study to the participants, informed consent was acquired. Before beginning and after the four-week ujjayi pranayama intervention, measurements of the thyroid profile and body mass index were taken. The gathered data was formatted in Microsoft Excel for analysis. Statistical analysis used: Using the SPSS 16 version of the software, both expressive and inferential statistical approaches were applied to the data analysis. Results: The patients' mean age among the participants was 49 ± 3.62, with 93% of the participants being female. In comparison to the pre-test evaluation, there was a substantial (p<0.001) decrease in the triiodothyronine and thyroxine scores, as well as a significant (p<0.001) reduction in the thyroid stimulating hormone and body mass index scores. Conclusion: Rendering to the consequences of the current study, Ujjain pranayama reduces body mass index and helps bring about desired changes in the thyroid profile within the therapeutic range.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Optimization Algorithm for Secure IoT Communication Using AMQP
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: This paper introduces a blockchain-based optimization algorithm that can be integrated with the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) to secure IoT communication. The proposed solution will overcome challenges such as decentralized trust, efficient message handling, and resource constraints in IoT systems. Our approach incorporates blockchain’s decentralized architecture, lightweight encryption mechanisms, and machine learning-based threat detection that offers real-time anomaly detection. Our method utilizes a dynamic consensus mechanism to adapt to the IoT network environment while making latency decreased and message throughput enhanced. Considering the experiment, it has been proven that better latency, throughput, security, and resource efficiency can be achieved. Smart homes, healthcare, and industrial IoT can be represented.

articleTitle: Advanced CNN-Based Approaches for COVID-19 Diagnosis and Multiclass Classification: An Experimental Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Early and precise diagnosis of various chronic chest disorders like COVID-19, Tuberculosis (TB), pneumonia, etc. is essential for efficient treatment planning. However, automatic detection and multiclass classification of these disorders present significant challenges due to the subtle radiographic features they exhibit. To address this challenge, we evaluated five CNN-based advanced deep learning (DL) models in order to categorize the input chest X-ray (CXR) images into COVID-19 infections (bacterial or viral), normal, and non-COVID-19. Initially, the input COVID-QU-Ex dataset (33,920 images) is pre-processed using image augmentation (rotation, flipping, shearing, etc.) to incorporate the possible variations and balance the class labels. Subsequently, contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) is employed to deal with poor contrast problem. Finally, we employed five DL models (VGG-16, VGG-19, ResNet-50, ResNet-18, ResNet-101) with finetuned parameters. The obtained experimental results indicate that ResNet-101 achieved highest performance (training accuracy=99.219%) in contrast to alternative models used in this study. The validation accuracy of 93.907% also confirmed the promins performance the proposed model. This study demonstrates DL’s prospective models to automate the diagnosis of chest diseases, offering valuable support to radiologists and enhancing diagnostic workflows.

articleTitle: Covid-19 detection from X-ray image using Deep learning and SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented a serious threat to world health. A precise and timely diagnosis is essential for successful treatment and containment. X-ray scans of the chest have become a promising method for COVID-19 early detection. This work suggests a novel method for extracting discriminative characteristics from X-ray scans by utilizing deep learning (DL),followed by classification using Support Vector Machines (SVM). By combining the robust feature extraction capabilities of deep learning models with the effectual classification power of SVM, we aim to develop a highly accurate and efficient COVID-19 detection system. This proposed method demonstrates promising results in accurately differentiating between COVID-19 +ve, COVID-19 -ve and pneumonia cases, offering a useful tool for healthcare experts. The proposed model shows the training accuracy of 98.72%, and test accuracy with 96.11% as the classification result.

articleTitle: Effect of Meditation on Varying Concentration in Non-meditators estimated through Hjorth Parameters of EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Practice of meditation reduces psychological stress of an individual, simultaneously increasing attention level. Dedicated practitioners of meditation are less affected by mental stress and also have a strong focus level. Non-meditators, on the other hand, cannot maintain their concentration at a fixed level. Due to this, they are more prone to stress as their minds constantly drift from one thought to the next. Also, practicing long-term meditation initially will be difficult for non-meditators. Instead, a brief and easy meditation form will be ideal for them. Focusing the breathing pattern of oneself for a brief period of time will serve as suitable meditation practice for non-meditators. This work observes the changes in brain waves of non-meditators while focusing on breathing for five minutes. To quantify changes in the human brain, the EEG signal needs to be studied as it provides insights into the underlying changes in the human brain during a particular phase. Analyzing statistical properties of EEG signals through Hjorth parameters evaluation assists in deciphering and understanding brain activity. In this work, the effect of breathe-focus meditation on concentration level in non-meditators has been observed by interpreting the changes of EEG signal through Hjorth parameters. From the results, it can be inferred that although concentration fluctuates in non-meditators, meditation still helps to reduce stress and enhance relaxation and concentration.

articleTitle: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis Disease Detection Through Facial Expression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Identifying Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) early is crucial for initiating treatment, improving prognosis, and enhancing the quality of life for affected individuals. However, early diagnosis and symptom detection can be challenging. A more accessible and cost-effective solution involves computational analysis of the patient’s facial expressions. ALS patients exhibit distinct facial muscle movements during specific actions, such as mouth opening, compared to healthy individuals. This paper proposes using deep learning-based facial expression analysis to detect ALS. The model was trained to recognize ALS symptoms through facial expression data and evaluated on the NeuroFace dataset. Experimental results show that the model achieved a high precision of 0.94, a recall of 0.89, and an F1-score of 0.92 for the ALS class. The overall accuracy of the model was 92%, demonstrating its effectiveness in distinguishing between ALS and healthy individuals, thus contributing to early ALS detection through non-invasive methods.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Bayesian Statistics for Healthcare Domain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: There has been a dramatic increase in the quantity of sensory input, which is enormous and diversified in structure, due to the adoption of smart gadgets and sensors to track healthcare patients. All of this is encompassed by the Internet of Things (IoT). Intelligence at a higher level is required for this data analysis to comprehend healthcare data patterns both now and in the future. Therefore, this research analyzes and evaluates the Bayesian statistics for detecting abnormalities in healthcare data. In particular, in the field of healthcare data monitoring, it enables us to follow the state of the current situation and predict future trends based on this knowledge. The experimental evaluation of this research work uses healthcare data for the evaluation of Bayesian statistics.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy BiLSTM Approach for Predicting COVID-19 Misinformation on Social Media Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The healthcare sector suffers from major outbreak of covid-19, this is a major pandemic also with misinformation that serves among online platform. This misinformation creates confusion among people for a longer period of time. Analyzing Covid-19 related misinformation is one of the major tasks in this work. Misinformation comes in various types this paper concentrate on one of the most common ways i.e., fake news. This work does the comparative analysis among different integrated algorithm like Bi-LSTM, Fuzzy Bi-LSTM, ARIMA, LSTM, stacked LSTM. These models are trained and tested on the publicly available dataset named "Fake News on COVID-19 Healthcare". Fuzzy Bi-LSTM is one of the methods that outperforms among the other model due to its capability of handling ambiguous data while doing sequential learning of Bi-LSTM. The Fuzzy Bi-LSTM compares using different evaluation metrics in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score which results 98.66

articleTitle: Transforming Pistachio Classification: The Power of ResNet-50 and SVM Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: In this study, a novel approach for Pistachio image classification is proposed, combining the feature extraction capabilities of the ResNet-50 convolutional neural network (CNN) with the classification power of a Support Vector Machine (SVM). The model was trained and evaluated on a dataset of 2148 Pistachio images, using 30 epochs to ensure optimal learning. The training process demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy during the initial 20 epochs, reaching a final training accuracy of 92.64% and a validation accuracy of 97.21%. The model’s loss values also exhibited steady decreases, indicating strong generalization to unseen data. The primary novelty of this research lies in the effective integration of deep feature extraction through ResNet-50 with SVM classification, providing high accuracy for agricultural image classification tasks.This approach demonstrates the potential for achieving robust Pistachio classification with fewer epochs, offering an efficient alternative to traditional CNN classifiers. Future research could explore larger datasets and alternative hybrid methods to further enhance classification performance. Additionally, testing the model’s applicability to other agricultural products could validate its generalizability across various domains.

articleTitle: Medical Data Analysis and Machine Learning Models for Kidney Disease Prediction: Exploratory Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Numerous recent breakthroughs in the field of ML and AI have made significant progress in the prediction and identification of healthcare catastrophes, disease communities, disease states, and immune system reactions. One characteristic of chronic kidney disease (CKD), sometimes referred to as chronic kidney failure, is a gradual decrease of the functioning of the kidneys. The Kidneys remove contaminants and surplus fluid from the bloodstream to produce urine. In the event of severe chronic renal illness, the human body may amass dangerously high levels of liquids, electrolytes, and toxic substances. The illness is called "chronic" because kidney damage in humans develops subsequently over a long period. Wastes may build up throughout your system as a result of this disease. These days, one of the most serious illnesses is CKD, for which a prompt diagnosis is essential. We use a variety of machine learning techniques in our current research to predict CKD. This work implements seven different ML algorithms to examine the kidney disease data and also finds the most suitable model. The results show that the three models Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting perform very well with an accuracy rate of 98.03%.

articleTitle: Developing Machine Learning Models to Detect Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in females, causing a significant amount of morbidity and mortality. In 2020, there were about 2.3 million new cases and 684,996 deaths worldwide. Early detection is critical, especially in younger women in India, where incidence rates are rising. This study explores the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for early-stage breast cancer detection and survival prediction using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset. It points out key characteristics of cell nucleus based on the feature extractions from FNA images of breast masses. Various distinct techniques of machine learning have been addressed in this study, including Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, and Logistic Regression. Out of these, Support Vector Machines and Logistic Regression produced similar results, with accuracy values of 98.24%. These results demonstrate the possibility of enhanced outcome measures and promotion of early diagnosis for the patients through machine learning.

articleTitle: Simulation of Venom Structures from Three Naja Species and Ophiophagus in the Philippines Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Snakebite envenoming is a potentially life- threatening disease caused by toxins from the bite of a venomous snake. Envenoming can also be caused by having venom sprayed into the eyes by certain species of snakes, such as the Naja sumatrana, these venomous snakes have the ability to spit venom as a defense measure. Communities from rural and agricultural areas in the Philippines are at high-risk towards the exposure of venomous snakes. However, the venom structures of Naja sumatrana, Naja philippinensis, Naja samarensis, and the Philippine population of Ophiophagus hannah are still poorly studied. This paper describes the utilization of artificial intelligence to simulate the venom structures of Naja sumatrana, Naja philippinensis, Naja samarensis, and the Philippine population of Ophiophagus hannah. Comparative analysis of the venom structures is also conducted to determine their toxin similarity. An understanding of the venom structure is important to determine the effectiveness of the available antivenom in the Philippines, as well as the medical potential of these venoms. By analyzing venom protein sequences, the deep learning model can predict the three-dimensional structures of venom toxins.

articleTitle: Development of a Markerless Augmented Reality Application for Plumbing Tool Training
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation and evaluation of a markerless augmented reality-based application for training using plumbing tools. Leveraging ARCore's environmental depth understanding and object tracking capabilities, the app utilizes 3D animations to walk users through practical experiences like cutting pipes with digital plumbing tools in their physical environment. The researchers conducted a comprehensive evaluation of the activities, which involved usability test on the application, user engagement and education effectiveness. The outcomes reveal a potential portal for tangible training with individuals who had experience using the app expressing higher levels of confidence about performing plumbing chores. Feedback on the AR experience was about an intuitive interaction and good visual guidance, with one feedback around bad frame rate (which researchers later found a couple of performance issues on lower end devices). Performance tweaks, further addition to the task library, and the most asked functionality assessments (test with guided procedures) are inputs. Taken together, this makes a strong case for AR as a transformational technology in job training and even creates the potential for new skilled trades and the careers on which are based on skills.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Conventional Systems and IoT-Edge Based Systems in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The integration of Edge Computing (EC) and the Internet of Things (IoT) offers a transformative approach to enhancing healthcare efficiency, particularly in real-time data processing and patient monitoring. By moving data computation near to the source, EC reduces bandwidth demands and latency, while IoT devices enable continuous, remote care. This study evaluates the impact of these technologies on patient outcomes, comparing them to conventional healthcare systems, and addressing challenges such as interoperability, privacy of data, and scalability. The results indicate that Edge-IoT solutions hold significant capabilities to bring revolutions for healthcare delivery, especially in response to global health crises.

articleTitle: RCS-YOLO: A Rapid and Precise Brain Tumor Detection Framework Utilizing the Adam Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Brain tumors are considered one of the most dangerous health issues, as they can spread quickly and significantly reduce a patient’s chances of survival if not treated promptly. Advanced YOLO frameworks are among the most efficient algorithms for object detection, yet their application in brain tumor detection has been limited. This paper presents a comprehensive strategy for identifying brain tumors using Robo-flow dataset and the existing RCS-YOLO method, enhanced by the RCS-OSA module. We improved accuracy by using the Adam optimizer, incorporating regularization techniques, and increasing the range of 150 to 200 training epochs, it outer-performed the method of Stochastic Gradient Descent. Using Hyperband tuner and the Adam optimizer, we achieved an impressive accuracy of 0.97, along with precision and recall scores of 0.97, indicating that the model generalizes well to unseen data. Our research shows cutting-edge results in the challenge of detecting brain tumors using Robo-flow database.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Classification of Medicinal Plant Leaf Diseases using CNNs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Over the past few decades, the application of neural networks in research has grown exponentially. Neural networks are widely used for diverse classification and identification tasks, including forensics and control management systems. They have also been explored in the context of plant leaf identification. This study proposes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based approach for the detection of diseases in medicinal plant leaves. Early detection of plant diseases is crucial to preventing pest infestations and minimizing their adverse effects on agriculture. Neural networks serve as powerful analytical classifiers, leveraging field images of plants to accurately identify and classify diseases, thus offering a highly efficient solution for agricultural diagnostics. Such techniques involve the identification and interpretation of huge picture databases, which are often impossible to do due to technological or financial constraints. In this work a fully automated method for the recognition and detection of disease in medicinal plants leaves using computer vision and machine learning techniques has been presented. Using ven-200 dataset the CNN model achieves accuracy of 98.57%, precision score of 93.51%, recall score of 95.67% and f1 score of 93.97% in 2500 epochs.

articleTitle: Improving EEG Signal Interpretation for Phoneme Classification through Residual Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Phoneme classification in speech imagery Brain-Computer Interfaces aims to decode imagined speech signals directly from brain activity, enabling communication without overt speech. This challenging task requires accurately distinguishing between various phonemes from complex, non-stationary EEG data, offering potential advancements in assistive communication technologies for individuals with speech impairments. This paper presents an approach for classifying phonemes in imagined speech tasks using EEG signals by employing an advanced deep learning model. The proposed methodology centers around a convolutional neural network architecture enhanced with residual connections, designed to improve classification performance by acquiring complex temporal and spatial patterns related to the EEG signals. Unlike conventional machine learning techniques, the residual connections enables the model to train deeper networks effectively, mitigating performance degradation even with a limited dataset. This approach is implemented using a speech imagery EEG dataset, achieving a marked improvement in classification accuracy over traditional methods. The results underscore the potential of this model for advancing multiclass phoneme classification in EEG-based brain-computer interface systems for future work towards imagined speech recognition.

articleTitle: Cloud Load Balancing Strategies for Optimizing Internet of Medical Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) applications has transformed healthcare delivery by enabling real-time monitoring and data exchange among medical devices. However, the increasing volume of data generated by these devices poses significant challenges in terms of performance, scalability, and reliability. Here are various cloud load balancing strategies aimed at optimizing IoMT applications. Rather than going through the several techniques we focused on the method of optimizing in depth (OID) by applying this method, we actually try to implement the series of optimization method that helps to optimize the utilization of cloud resources in more efficient manner. Our findings demonstrate that dynamic load balancing significantly improves resource utilization and reduces latency, thereby enhancing the overall user experience. By implementing geographic load balancing, we also highlight the potential for reduced latency and improved response times for users accessing IoMT applications from diverse locations. This research contributes to the existing body of knowledge by providing actionable insights into cloud load balancing strategies that can effectively support the evolving landscape of IoMT applications, ultimately leading to improved healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: From Notes to Nodes: Patient-Centric Knowledge Graph for Targeted Glaucoma Care
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Unstructured clinical notes, often composed of free-text descriptions by healthcare providers, are rich in detailed patient information but lack a consistent format, making them challenging to analyze. Integrating Knowledge graphs (KG) into healthcare provides significant advantages, especially in managing chronic conditions like glaucoma. The treatment decisions for such cases depend on various clinical factors. KGs are an essential tool for modeling complex healthcare relationships. It provides a structured and interpretable framework for understanding medical concepts and their connections. The graph structure enhances NLP techniques, efficiently extracting critical information from unstructured clinical data. This paper presents the Patient-Centric Knowledge Graph (PaCKG). It is constructed from unstructured clinical notes focusing on glaucoma patients. Our method, PaCKG, aims to help clinicians make medical decisions by mapping relationships between patients, their symptoms, and corresponding treatments. The PaCKG follows three steps. First, preprocessing the clinical notes; second, Extracting relevant information using Named Entity Recognition (NER); and finally, Constructing the KG, which includes three main node types—patients, symptoms, and treatments (drugs). By structuring unstructured clinical notes, PaCKG enables efficient retrieval and relational mapping of critical healthcare information. The key metrics analyzed include the total number of nodes, symptoms, treatments, and the total number of edges and relationships. Further insights are derived from the average degree, degree distribution, and the number of weakly connected components, which provide a comprehensive view of the graph’s structure. Performance is demonstrated through accurate extraction of symptoms and treatments, along with high connectivity and appropriate density of links, effectively linking patients to their symptoms and treatments in the knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Phonocardiogram Signal Based Better Prediction of Aortic and Mitral Stenosis Heart Diseases Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Valvular Heart Disease (VHD), is a major cause of mortality and morbidity. Even though echocardiography is the most accurate method of diagnosing VHD, not everyone has access to this equipment. It is not sufficient to use manual cardiac auscultation for VHD screening. Since several machine learning models incorporate heart sounds captured with an electronic stethoscope, the diagnosis of VHD may be more precise. Heart valve disorders such as Mitral Stenosis (MS) and Aortic Stenosis (AS) can be detected from the PCG signal. Our goal was to develop an accurate heart sound classification algorithm for severity of AS and MS diagnosis. The approach suggested combines machine learning methods with conventional features. Features are retrieved from PCG signals using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Wavelet Packet Transform (WPT), and Perceptual Wavelet Packet Transform (PWPT) techniques. Neighborhood Component Analysis (NCA) technique is applied to all features and the best features are selected. we employ multiple machine learning approaches, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms. Hyper-parameter optimization is used to train machine learning models in order to improve classification accuracy. In addition, we use our own built-in device to collect PCG signals from renowned heart specialists in Kolkata that have valvular heart diseases in order to confirm the detection of AS and MS with varying degrees of severity (severe AS, mild AS, mild MS, and moderate MS). We then validate the results using our method. In this analysis, the average accuracy of RF, SVM, DT, and KNN were 99.2%, 99%, 98%, and 98.4%, respectively. These results might potentially be useful in multiclass problems involving the classification of stenosis illnesses. The proposed method shows great potential in providing detection of VHD and save the patients from severe cardiac issue.

articleTitle: In silico analysis of deleterious p53 SNPs in Parkinson’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Tumor suppressor p53 is a transcription factor associated with apoptosis or programmed cell death as it is responsible for activating several caspases and downstream apoptotic signaling cascades which leads to cell death. Apoptosis is crucial for maintaining different cellular and biological processes within the organism like genome stability and integrity and cell cycle regulation. Apoptosis plays a major role in progression of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) like Parkinson’s disease (PD) where substantial loss of neuronal cells which secrete Dopamine takes place mediated by upregulated expression of p53 protein. In this study we have targeted the missense single nucleotide polymorphs (msSNPs) of p53 which are not reported to be significantly associated with any disease using in silico analysis tools. Structural stability and evolutionary studies have identified eight SNPs to be the most conserved which were further used in this study. All eight variants were found to be most deleterious in accordance with their docking score with MDM2 (inhibitor of p53), which theoretically suggests that apoptosis in cells with these p53 mutations may be less due to high binding affinity of the variants towards MDM2 and thus provide a new insight about potential therapeutic strategies for treating NDDs like PD.

articleTitle: Predicting Criticality of Patients Based on Disease Symptoms Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Predicting disease criticality is essential for immediate medical attention and optimizing healthcare facilities. In this work, we propose a Machine Learning (ML) based approach to predict the criticality of a patient based on disease symptoms. By using Disease-Symptom Knowledge Database dataset, we created a binary classification model to distinguish critical conditions of a patient from non-critical ones. For this, multiple classification algorithms are employed to achieve optimal accuracy and among them the Gradient Boosting (GB) classifier was found to give best result with 95.71% accuracy. The study also includes Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) to understand the symptom-disease relationships.

articleTitle: Swish-Enhanced Hybrid Model for Alzheimer’s Diagnosis Using VGG16 and ResNet50 on MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease is an extreme neurological illness that deteriorates over time, affecting memory, communication, and mental skills resulting in irreversible brain damage. Early detection is key, as timely treatment can help manage symptoms and slow down the progress of the disease. We created a hybrid deep learning model combining the VGG16 and ResNet50 architectures to classify brain MRI images into ‘Demented’ and ‘Nondemented’ groups. We also used the Swish activation function, which provides smoother gradients and improved performance than ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit). Through the use of k – fold cross – validation, the model’s average accuracy was 89.79% and final test accuracy was 91.44%. Other evaluation measures, like recall, precision and F1 – score, all showed an average of 0.91 for both classes, showing that the network works good on unseen data. While this work focuses on binary classification, future research will expand to multi – class classification to detect several phases of cognitive decline.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of PO, SO and SHO Algorithms for Epileptic Seizer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Diseases originated due to the disorder in the neurons present in the brain part of the body is called epilepsy and the symptom observed in other parts of the body is called a seizure. Not only it is a typical disease in human beings but animals are also suffered from this disease. To live an epilepsy-free life, neurologists and researchers contribute their best effort to devise new techniques and presently metaheuristic optimization algorithms and machine learning algorithms are integrated into this field to design powerful EEG devices for accurately detecting the presence of EEG signals. This research paper presents the comparison of three metaheuristic optimization algorithms used in designing EEG detection. In addition, these three algorithms are integrated with Extreme Learning Adoptive Neuro-Fuzzy-Inference System (ELANFIS) as the classifier and Wavelet Packet Transform as the feature extraction technique. For continuing research work, this experiment uses the Bonn University EEG dataset. After a thorough analysis, it is observed that WPT-PO-ELANFIS is the best-performing technique among these three with average accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under curve values as 98.42, 96.75, 97.97.97.65, and 0.989. This research work also can be tested with other popularly available datasets and integrated with real-time applications.

articleTitle: A Secure Architecture Utilizing Blockchain Based Edge Computing for E-Anganwadi System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Anganwadi establishments play a crucial role in providing rural communities with vital healthcare and nutrition services, yet they frequently contend with shortcoming in security and ineffective digital data processing. This article integrates blockchain technology with edge computing to present a safe e-Anganwadi system framework. By shifting computation to the edge of the network, edge computing speeds up data processing, reduces latency, and lessens need on cloud infrastructure. Blockchain technology, on the other hand, guarantees safe and unchangeable record-keeping, encouraging openness and confidence in sensitive data transactions. By strengthening resistance against various attacks and data breaches, the decentralized architecture guarantees dependable and consistent service delivery. For the purpose of updating Anganwadi services in remote and underprivileged areas, this framework offers a reliable, safe, and effective alternative.

articleTitle: FedProx-Based Federated Transfer Learning for Efficient Model Personalization in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates collaborative model training among multiple clients at diverse locations while preserving data privacy, making it particularly suitable for healthcare applications. Nevertheless, conventional (FL) techniques often face challenges such as significant communication overhead and unstable convergence, especially when dealing with heterogeneous data. To address these challenges, we propose a FedProx-based Federated Transfer Learning (FTL) framework that leverages pre-trained models to improve convergence stability with less training. The proposed method introduces a proximal regularization term that penalizes large updates to local models, thereby ensuring model robustness across different hospitals. The use of pre-trained models further reduces the amount of local data needed for training, enabling effective personalization with limited datasets. Experiments on a synthetic healthcare dataset demonstrate that our method achieves comparable performance to traditional FL methods while significantly improving convergence and learning capability, making it suitable for resource-constrained healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Pneumonia detection and classification from chest X-Ray images using Modified DenseNet121 Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Pneumonia is a potential life-threatening lung infection that remains a global health concern even today. Adequate diagnosis in time is essential to improve therapeutic results. In this study, we present a modified deep learning-based approach "transfer learning" for automatic identification of pneumonia in chest X-ray images. Utilizing transfer learning with pre-trained DenseNet121 model and leveraging the feature extraction capabilities, we fine-tuned them with additional connected layers specifically tailored for binary classification to distinguish between pneumonia normal and positive cases. We have applied data augmentation techniques to expand the small dataset and enhance model generalization. The modified model is trained with training and validated with respective datasets. Our proposed modified DenseNet121 model achieved classification accuracy of 90.06%, with a sensitivity of 0.89 and specificity of 0.90 with testing datasets. These metrics indicate that the model is highly effective in identifying pneumonia cases from X-ray images. The proposed approach has remarkable potential for clinical use, providing a reliable, automated solution for assisting radiologists in diagnosing pneumonia, which could help reduce the diagnostic burden in resource-constrained environments and improve patient outcomes. Overall, this method combines the power of transfer learning, augmentation, and fine-tuning to deliver higher accuracy and offers a way for quick preliminary automated pneumonia detection.

articleTitle: Burnout Syndrome and Coping Strategies among Nursing Staff: Modeling and Prototyping a Smart Prevention System Using the Internet of Medical Things
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The aim of this research is to propose a prototype mobile recommendation system that leverages exploiting the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) for real-time health monitoring and burnout assessment among healthcare professionals. The system is designed not only to assess burnout, but also to provide personalized coping strategies. The system architecture was conceptualized using the Unified Modeling Language (UML). The prototype integrates various biometric sensors such as, including electrocardiogram (ECG), blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation and temperature, in conjunction with psychometric tests to assess burnout syndrome. By continuously monitoring physiological and psychological parameters, this system offers significant benefits for promoting the general well-being of healthcare professionals. In addition to its real-time monitoring capabilities, it serves as a preventive tool to alleviate stress, detect early signs of burnout and reduce the risk of developing chronic illnesses. This holistic approach addresses both mental and physical health, providing a comprehensive solution to the growing problem of burnout in the healthcare sector. The proposed system aims to improve the quality of life and job satisfaction of healthcare professionals, by strengthening their resilience in the face of professional stress factors.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification Using Feature Extraction Techniques: A Comparative Study of Local Binary Patterns (LBP) and the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) with Random Forest Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Brain tumors are atypical proliferations within the brain that may pose a significant threat to life, necessitating prompt and precise diagnosis to enhance patient prognoses and facilitate successful intervention. This work uses MRI data to identify and classify brain tumors using machine learning techniques, including Random Forest and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms. MRI images are denoised, enhanced, and standardized before meaningful features, such as texture patterns, shapes, and statistical characteristics, are extracted. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used to decrease dimensionality and improve computational efficiency. Using Random Forest in combination with advanced feature extraction techniques like GLCM, LBP, and PCA, the models achieved an impressive 95% accuracy rate with precision, recall, and F1-scores 0.95, outperforming the SVM model, which achieved a consistent but modest accuracy of 76%. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating feature engineering and machine learning in complex medical diagnostics. The proposed method is well-suited for real-time clinical applications and automated brain tumor detection pipelines, offering a robust approach to enhancing diagnostic accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: COVIS-Health: A Deep Learning and Explainable AI-Based Decision Support System for Identification of COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Early-stage identification of COVID-19 authentically is a critical task for doctors. Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) is a more reliable, helpful, and quick method of classifying and evaluating COVID- 19 cases and was widely used during the pandemic. This method does not talk about the severity level of the disease; on the other hand, medical image- based methods like Computed Tomography (CT) of the chest tell a lot about the severity level. This research paper attempts to develop a Corona Virus Identification System for Health known as COVIS-Health for COVID-19 identification using chest CT image data. In order to develop a Decision Support System, Deep learning techniques like Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with hyper-parameters tuning, transfer learning, dual transfer learning, and augmentation were used along with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), which was added at the last layer of CNN to explain the severity level of infection. Experimental results reveal that dual transfer learning and the augmented-based VGG-19 model along with XAI outperform other CNN models by more than 99% accuracy. The developed COVIS-Health system allows end users to upload CT scan image data to identify it as COVID- 19 positive or negative. Apart from this, it also explains the severity level of any COVID-19 infected patients.

Author Keywords: Corona Virus Identification System for Health (COVIS- Health)

articleTitle: Predicting disease in rose leaves using improvised ResNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Currently, the growing demand for flowers has led to their commercial cultivation worldwide. Therefore, the farmers are investing in it due to its numerous benefits. The rose (Genus Rosa) is the most demanding of the flowers, as it has the most beautiful and loving fragrance. However, insecticide resistance is one of the critical issues farmers face in the agricultural production of roses. Insecticide resistance stunts the growth of the plants, leading to a quality issue. Furthermore, the number of healthy-looking roses is decreasing. As a result, roses are becoming less well-known in terms of quality and production due to numerous environmental and natural problems. Furthermore, farmers who invest in rose production are not sufficiently educated to recognize the initial infections in the leaves. Poor communication skills, rather than production estimation, exacerbate the situation, particularly when farmers seek timely advice from an agriculturist. Early identification of infection would help the farmers control the growth of the infection in the rose leaves, which is very crucial. Deep learning models have emerged as the most effective methods for detecting various diseases through leaf images, and they also serve numerous other purposes. In this paper, we have proposed a deep-learning model to build a rose leaf disease prediction system. With the proposed model, 98.78% accuracy is achieved using the RoseNet dataset, which contains the images of three classes: blackspot, downy mildew, and fresh leaf.

articleTitle: Digitization and Classification of Electrocardiograms for Automated Cardiovascular Disease Diagnosis Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Electrocardiograms (ECG) enable the straightforward identification of cardiovascular diseases (CVD). However, the complexity of ECG graphs often challenges physicians in making precise and confident diagnoses. This study aims to digitize electrocardiograms using a publicly available ECG image dataset from the Mendeley database and classify the signals into four categories: normal, arrhythmia, myocardial infarction (MI), and past myocardial infarction (PMI). The proposed framework includes a comprehensive preprocessing pipeline involving greyscale conversion, noise elimination, segmentation, and normalization. The classification process employs advanced deep learning models like EfficientNet-1D and ResNet-1D alongside machine learning (ML) models such as XGBoost, Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, and k-Nearest Neighbours (kNN). The models were evaluated using performance metrics, including F1-score, accuracy, recall, and precision. The Voting Ensemble Classifier outperformed achieving the highest overall accuracy of 93.2%. Among the deep learning models, ResNet-1D achieved an accuracy of 86.6%, while EfficientNet-1D attained 92.2%, demonstrating strong performance in ECG classification. ResNet-1D excelled in detecting normal and arrhythmic signals, while EfficientNet-1D demonstrated superior effectiveness in identifying myocardial infarctions. Both models exhibited high precision and recall, with ResNet-1D achieving exceptional success. This study underscores the importance of digitizing printed ECG records for advanced medical diagnostics and highlights the role of performance metrics in evaluating model efficacy. The proposed method enhances ECG classification accuracy and is well-suited for real-time clinical applications and automated cardiac disease detection systems.

articleTitle: Reducing Complexity in Drug-Target Interaction Studies: Framework for Descriptor Subset Selection using Deep Clustering and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The plethora of publicly available molecular descriptors poses a potential risk of encountering the 'curse of dimensionality,' which can significantly complicate the resolution of high-dimensional challenges such as drug discovery rooted in chemical space. In drug-target interaction analysis, the comprehensive RDKit database comprising more than 20,000 descriptors contributes to an enormous complexity in selecting, reducing, and building models. To alleviate this complexity, meticulous subset selection, evaluation, and validation of clustering and classification analyses are imperative. The study focuses on the relative importance of various molecular descriptors in drug-target interactions for three immune targets: Collagenase-3 (MMP-13), STAT1-alpha/beta isoform alpha (STAT-1), and NF-kB p105 subunit isoform1 (NF-kB). The study utilized a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) with K-means clustering, a Cluster-Generative Adversarial Network (ClusterGAN) based DL clustering algorithm, and a Fully Connected Neural Network (FCNN) for classification tasks. Experiments were conducted utilizing the entire RDKit descriptor set, RDKit descriptors subjected to Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and domain-specific subsets. The findings revealed that, in clustering tasks, domain-based subset selection marginally enhances performance when sufficient data are available. Conversely, classification accuracy is adversely impacted by subset selection and dimensionality reduction.

articleTitle: Enhanced Stroke Risk Prediction with XGBoost Classifier: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Stroke remains a significant global health challenge, necessitating accurate risk prediction models for effective prevention and management. This study adopts a transfer learning approach to improve the prediction of stroke risk using the XGBoost classifier, which is strong and reliable. Since stroke datasets naturally tend to be imbalanced between class types, the SMOTE procedure was used during the preprocessing stage to reduce the bias in the stroke and non-stroke distributions. The study aims to achieve good prediction results based on demographic, lifestyle, and medical history data. Analytically, the research steps through data preprocessing through SMOTE, model building with XGBoost classifier, and thorough assessment using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The study highlights the importance of the XGBoost classifier in diagnosing the risk of stroke more efficiently than conventional approaches. For instance, the model offered an accuracy of 93.05 percent in identifying the preferred communication medium. Furthermore, the work defines potential predictors that are significant in increasing stroke incidence, which is useful in the context of the establishment of individual prevention measures. The present work makes significant steps towards the further development of the concept of individual-specific medical treatment of diseases and public health programs after a stroke.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Approaches for Improved Detection and Diagnosis of Pancreatic Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Pancreatic Cancer, although one of the most dangerous cancers, has an unfavorable prognosis because of the fact that there are no particular symptoms and it is usually diagnosed on a later stage. This review discusses the possibilities offered by artificial intelligence and especially machine learning and deep learning techniques for the enhancement of detecting and diagnosing pancreatic cancer. The review emphasizes advanced AI models for pancreatic tumor’s classification and outlining which include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as well as segmentation methods. These AI enhanced approaches aim at achieving accurate, early diagnosis by integrating multiple image modalities including contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and histopathological images as well as biomarkers CA19-9 and genetic information. Besides, the paper analyses some optimization methods that ensure model performance and data security in a cooperative multi-institutional environment, such as federated learning and genetic algorithms. It is also important to consider how intelligence can reduce misdiagnosis, reduce the number of clinics, and save money for patients. This article addresses the challenges in image analysis, provides a comprehensive review of AI applications in cancer diagnosis, and offers suggestions for future research on how to create AI systems that can be easily integrated.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction in Healthcare Utilizing Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is among the most dangerous conditions that many people suffer from. Age, obesity, poor food, heredity, high blood pressure, and inactivity are some of the variables that might lead to diabetes mellitus. Though there are additional forms of diabetes, such as gestational diabetes, which appears during pregnancy, the two most common types are type 1 and type 2. In data science, machine learning is a relatively new field of study that looks at how machines pick up knowledge via experience. The goal of this work is to build a system that can more accurately forecast a patient's risk of developing diabetes in their early years by utilizing a combination of research data and machine learning techniques. Interpretable findings using logistic regression (LR) show how various risk variables affect the chance of acquiring diabetes. The most crucial characteristics for diabetes prediction may be automatically discovered by neural networks (NN) from unprocessed input data, eliminating the requirement for human feature selection. While compared to previous models, both the logistic regression and the neural network in this study provide a respectable accuracy score following a 10-fold classification.

articleTitle: Emotional Well-being of a Human: A Case Study of Proposing a Digital Twin Solution Integrating IoT Sensors and Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: There are many different types of technology that can improve well-being and quality of life through monitoring, comprehension, and continuous feedback. One such technology is the digital twin. Consequently, employing a digital twin as a type of solution can improve an individual's emotional health and quality of life in a surrounding environment. But it will take some time to develop digital twin systems that can make it easier to create and use digital twins because there are many variables that can affect how a digital twin is designed, including the kind of sensor, complementary technologies, the context of the situation being assessed for the person, and the surrounding environment. In this paper, we describe a real-time hybrid sensor fusion strategy for environmental factors, such as temperature, humidity and brightness with respect to an individual's heart rate monitoring using machine learning models such as random forest, linear regression and ridge regression. Further, Explainable AI-SHAP is utilized to enhance the interpretability of the machine learning models, hence guaranteeing the credibility and understanding of the digital twin's predictions in this study. These methods put the idea of real- time feedback to use by introducing a digital twin for emotions of human into practice.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Biomarker Discovery in Lung Cancer: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: The discovery of cancer biomarkers is essential for early diagnosis, individualised care, and better patient outcomes. With an emphasis on lung cancer in particular, this paper provides an analysis of various ML techniques for identification of cancer biomarkers. To find cancer biomarkers from complex omics data, various ML algorithms are being studied, such as ensemble methods, deep learning, supervised learning, and unsupervised learning. This study reviews recent research, analysing how these methods are applied to tackle challenges in feature extraction, feature selection, and data integration. We highlight the promise of ML in discovering robust biomarkers that can significantly improve cancer prognosis, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes. Furthermore, the paper acknowledges existing challenges, such as data variability and limited interpretability of complex models, while discussing future advancements. These include incorporating multi-omics data for deeper insights, developing explainable AI models, and enhancing data integration techniques to improve early cancer detection and personalised therapeutic strategies.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Approaches for Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using Indian and Multi-Centric Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis affects 10-15% of the global population over the age of 60, mostly women. Knee osteoarthritis is growing more widespread in India due to changing lifestyle choices, rising urbanisation, and demographics. Furthermore, many serious cases in India go untreated since many believe it is only a concern for the elderly. Additionally, the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis has been difficult in rural India due to a lack of skilled medical professionals. Additionally, people are ignorant of its severity, as evidenced by KL's grading system, which ranges from normal to severe (Grades 0-4). This study compares various deep learning architectures and their performance metrics in order to analyze the effectiveness of deep learning-based prediction models for knee osteoarthritis detection. This study utilized an Indian dataset because there is limited research conducted on Indian subjects. The OAI and MOST datasets, which comprise data from Western people, were used in the majority of the investigations. This is the first study, in which we compare the effects of knee osteoarthritis using three distinct datasets. In the study, various pre-trained CNN-based models for 5-class and 2-class classification was used. On an Indian dataset, the EfficientNetB1 model achieved testing accuracy of 84% and EfficientNetB7 on a 2-class classification achieved accuracy of 90.2%. Subsequently, 61% and 77.7% of the western dataset's accuracy comes from 5-class and 2-class categorization using VGG-19 model, respectively. Furthermore, the accuracy of the multi-centric dataset using EfficientNetB1, B7 for 5-class classification is 61%, whereas for 2-class classification it is 80.82% respectively.

articleTitle: Predicting Stroke Risk Using Random Forest Classifier: A Healthcare Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: This work explores the Random Forest classifier's effectiveness in analyzing healthcare data for predicting stroke risks. In this study, data preprocessing is done intensively, which ranges from handling missing values, encoding categorical variables, and handling class imbalance, where the data is oversampled using SMOTE to balance the data between stroke and no-stroke cases. After preprocessing, the proposed approach uses the Random Forest classifier to predict the possibility of a stroke in people for the processed data. Further, features related to model selection and characteristics, including a grid search that incorporates cross-validation, are used to fine-tune the classifier for the best results. The performance of the developed Random Forest model is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Moreover, the interpretability of the model is examined to determine which factors affect stroke prediction. The results prove that the Random Forest classifier has high potential in the prediction of stroke risks with 94.42% accuracy, using advanced model selection and tuning techniques. Therefore, this study contributes towards clinical applications employing the Random Forest method, especially when applied with a preprocessing approach such as SMOTE, which can be beneficial in clinical settings for its ability to assess stroke risk mutually with approaches pertinent for healthcare practitioners and academics.

articleTitle: Ensemble Machine Learning Model for Detection of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: A type of motor neuron disease is called amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Its symptoms include breathing difficulties and a lack of control over the arms and legs, and it is detected by the nerve cells in the nervous system and the spine and early medical intervention, better disease management, research advancements, clinical trial enrolment, using the Ensemble Machine Learning has significant advantages for ALS patients. It emphasizes the potential for machine learning techniques to assist in the early diagnosis of challenging disorders like ALS, which would be advantageous for the healthcare sector. Early detection of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis enhancing the health and quality of life of a patient and helping patients and caregivers overcome the difficulties brought on by this terrible illness are all priorities. Although, using other Supervised learning which gives results about detection of neuron disorder, it is presumed that Ensemble Machine Learning provides better conclusions.

articleTitle: Data Anomalies and Outlier Detection in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Statistical Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: To forecast anomalies in the diagnosis of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), 400 cases with 25 attributes (11 numerical and 14 nominal) are taken from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Missing values in numerical and nominal features are addressed by mean and mode imputation techniques respectively. In present work, two methods are utilized to identify outliers: Z-score and the Interquartile Range (IQR). The Z-score method is used to identify extreme departures from the mean; it has shown particularly helpful in identifying outliers in characteristics such as blood pressure and serum creatinine. IQR method, on the other hand identified outliers in traits like age and blood sugar. Using a dual-method approach, this study produces a complete framework for identifying anomalies in data related to Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). The techniques clarify the existence and severity of CKD by examining the distribution of patient data, which makes early diagnosis and disease progression tracking possible.

articleTitle: The Deep Learning Based Analysis and Prediction of Apple Black Rot Disease in Apple Plants using ResNet-50 Hybrid Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Apple black rot, caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, significantly impacts apple trees, causing notable crop damage. This disease appears as black, sunken spots on fruits, leaves, and branches. Early signs include small, purple spots on leaves that expand and darken. Infected fruits develop concentric decay rings, known as "frogeye" spots. The fungus survives winter in mummified fruits and dead wood, spreading via wind and rain. Effective control involves removing and destroying infected material, using appropriate fungicides, and maintaining orchard cleanliness. Prompt detection and intervention are essential to prevent severe outbreaks and maintain healthy apple yields. This study introduces a deep-learning classifier designed to distinguish between two types of image data, one showing apple leaves affected by apple black rot disease and the other showing healthy apple leaves. The images undergo de-noising to improve quality. The cleaned data is then used to train ResNet-50 networks, achieving high precision. In summary, this research aims to develop a highly accurate image classifier for detecting apple black rot disease, achieving an accuracy rate of 95.86%.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Based Framework to Classify Parkinson Disease using Voice Signal and HandDraw
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder characterized by late-stage symptoms that significantly impact patients' quality of life. Early diagnosis and treatment of PD are crucial for alleviating symptoms and slowing disease progression. However, accurately diagnosing PD is challenging due to the overlap of its symptoms with those of other disorders. This study proposes a multimodal framework that leverages voice signals and handwritten graphics for the diagnosis of PD. The approach involves preprocessing and segmentation of speech signals to spectrogram and the binarization of handwritten graphics (circle, spiral, and meander) for analysis, incorporating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Three pre-trained deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) and an attention-based neural network model were trained on both datasets. The integration of speech signals and HandDraw images facilitated a comprehensive multimodal analysis. The proposed DCNN with an attention network achieved a classification accuracy of 98.75% on the multimodal dataset, outperforming other state-of-the-art approaches. These results demonstrate the potential of the framework for improving PD diagnosis.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Relapse Prediction Using Self-Organizing Maps: A Clustering-Based Approach for Early Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Lung cancer relapse is very often found to affect patient prognosis and treatment outcomes potentially and may lead to more challenging management and poorer survival rates. Early prediction of relapse is necessary for timely intervention and personalized treatment plans and to handle the key effects of relapse on prognosis and treatment, such as prognosis and survival, treatment outcomes, impact on treatment strategies, psychosocial effects, and potential for clinical trials. With this motivation, this paper proposed Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to predict lung cancer relapse. The SOM technique is considered for predicting lung cancer relapse due to its dimensionality reduction, ability to recognize and cluster patterns, visual way to interpret complex medical data operation without the need for labelled training data, capability to handle non-linear relationships, adaptability to evolving data, and noise tolerance. It is investigated that this unsupervised learning technique clusters patients based on their clinical and pathological features, providing a valuable tool for identifying relapse-prone patients. The results reflect that the proposed approach attains high prediction accuracy by leveraging the clustering capabilities of SOMs and effectively classifying patients into relapse and non-relapse categories. It can be concluded that the SOMs have the potential to enhance early detection and personalized treatment of lung cancer relapse.

articleTitle: Pneumonia Detection using Chest X-Ray Images: A Convolutional Neural Network with Skip Connection Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: Pneumonia is a lung infection, that causes breathing difficulties and significant risks to young children, older persons, and individuals with weak immune systems. Diagnosing pneumonia typically involves examining chest X-rays to identify abnormal white patches over the lung area that indicate infection. This study addresses the diagnosis of pneumonia using artificial intelligence techniques, thereby reducing the need for extensive human intervention and saving time in pneumonia diagnosis. To achieve this, we developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with skip connection blocks. These skip connections help the model retain critical information and accelerate convergence thus eliminating the vanishing gradient problem. The model was trained on 5,863 chest radiograph images, achieving outstanding accuracy, precision, and recall scores of 96.76%, 97.56%, and 98.01%, respectively. This high performance ensures accurate pneumonia identification, in the areas where precise diagnosis is crucial, such as in healthcare facilities. The study's findings emphasize the effectiveness of residual blocks in improving CNN performance for medical image analysis. To emphasise the effectiveness of our model we have also implemented comparative study with other established models including InceptionV3, ResNet50 and VGG-16. Proposed model demonstrated superiority in convergence time and model parameter efficiency. By reducing training iterations, our model expedites the diagnostic process and underscores the potential of AI in rapid medical diagnostics. This pioneering research establishes a strong foundation for future studies aimed at leveraging AI in diagnosing a variety of medical conditions using X-ray imaging. It has the potential to revolutionize medical diagnostics through advanced computational techniques.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection from Leaf Images Utilizing Ensemble Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: For agricultural productivity maximization and economic loss reduction, accurate and rapid identification of plant diseases is essential. This study introduces a state-of-the-art ensemble learning approach to disease classification in plants using images of their leaves. Here, two pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) serve as the basis for the classifiers, utilizing the benefits of deep CNNs. Using the pictures of the leaves, these base classifiers pull out general characteristics. After that, to get a good picture of the illness patterns, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) combines the features that were retrieved from the two CNNs. Overfitting the training data is less likely to happen with an ensemble design, which improves generalization. The internet application acknowledges user-uploaded pictures, forms them, and provides real-time expectations alongside a visual representation of the input picture. Moreover, the framework guarantees compatibility with different picture resolutions and keeps up a secure record taking care of the instrument. This system serves as a profitable apparatus for ranchers, analysts, and rural specialists, advertising an available arrangement to distinguish plant maladies expeditiously. By moderating the challenges of manual assessment and progressing symptomatic precision, the framework contributes to economical rural homes and improved nourishment generation efficiency. The proposed approach provided 98.05% testing accuracy that showcases the efficacy of the ensemble learning method in identifying plant diseases.

articleTitle: Advancing Healthcare with GPGPU and Energy Efficient NoC Architectures: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Ambient Intelligence in Health Care (ICAIHC)
abstract: General-purpose Graphics Processing Units (GPGPU) have emerged as a transformative technology in healthcare and medical fields, harnessing their powerful parallel processing capabilities to handle complex computational challenges. Initially developed for graphics rendering, GPUs are now employed in high-performance tasks such as medical imaging, genomic analysis, drug discovery, and real-time patient monitoring, where vast data volumes and intensive computations are prevalent. GPGPU technology enhances processing efficiency, reduces latency, and supports faster, more accurate diagnostics and treatment planning. Complementing this advancement, Networks-On-Chip (NoC) designs, introduced in the early 2000s, have become a standard communication backbone for high-end CPUs and Systems-on-Chip (SoCs). Their low communication latency, high throughput, and energy efficiency make NoCs ideal for addressing the growing demands of GPU-based systems. However, achieving these performance objectives requires minimizing power dissipation, energy consumption, and costs. This research provides a comprehensive survey of NoC design models for multi-GPU systems, focusing on their role in energy-efficient and scalable architectures.
